opening_message:
Ticket 1: Karen Alexander (employee ID E030) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E030.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Employee E030 (Karen Alexander) is a full-time Analyst. Requested write access to Source Code, which is at the maximum allowed level for full-time employees without owning-role admin. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E030 (Karen Alexander) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors max out at read without advanced training; requested write exceeds max, so recommend read.
reason: Conflicting records exist for E030: HR note lists full-time Analyst (would permit write), while Security note lists contractor with basic security training (max = read; write exceeds max and is not allowed without advanced training). Given the direct conflict on employment type and to stay within policy under the more restrictive interpretation, grant read — the maximum permitted for a contractor with basic training and a level that is policy-compliant under both records.
